newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat Varazdinska sees price rising after listing.
newsitem.headline: Croat Varazdinska sees price rising after listing.

text.p: Croatian commercial bank Varazdinska Banka, which signed an agreement on Thursday to list its shares on Zagreb's bourse, said it hoped this move would draw investors and lift its share price.
"We cannot guess at this stage what the market capitalisation will be, but hope that the price of our shares will rise now," bank president Mato Lukinic told a news conference.
A solid 1996 profit, forecast at around 28 million kuna after tax, and planned expansion of its services would be good reasons to invest in Varazdinska, he said.
Its ordinary and preferred shares with a total face value of 175 million kuna are expected to start trading on the Zagreb Stock Exchange next Tuesday.
Extremely short supply recently propelled the price of its 16,000 kuna face value ordinary stock to 42,000 kuna.
Preferred shares last traded at more than double their 500 kuna nominal price on the over-the-counter market.
The bank will propose a share split to its shareholders at an annual meeting later this month, after which both series are to be reissued at 100 kuna per share.
If approved, the split is seen improving liquidity and additionally encouraging trade.
"We believe this will also boost the price by a few percent," Lukinic said.
He added that Varazdinska is mulling steps to list its shares in London under the guidance of its shareholder -- the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
It will become the third Croatian firm to get a listing abroad after drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka.
